_readme: WHO SOLD THE PACKS AND WHERE HE BOUGHT THEM, for the rips whose description
does not say it in the shape the automatic join needs. Keyed by YouTube video id.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL, given both joins are automatic. They read the
rip's own description, and they are deliberately strict: shared/pack-source.mjs
needs an @handle, because 'go follow @X' and a bare name are the same string to
a handle search and only one of them is a credit; shared/bought-at.mjs needs the
town, because 'CollectorFest Monthly' in Rochester, NY and 'Collectorfest' in
SYRACUSE are two different shows and it credited the wrong one before that gate
went in. Strictness is right, and it means a description that says 'from TOAK
Pulls' in plain text yields nothing at all. That happened on 2 September 2026.
THE OWNER IS THE SOURCE HERE, NOT AN INFERENCE, and that is the whole licence
for this file. Every entry records what he said and when. Do NOT add a row
because a description looks like it means a shop, or because a show was on that
weekend: that is exactly the guessing both joins refuse to do. If it is not on
the record, leave it out and the page says nothing, which is the standing rule.
seller  the YouTube handle on the vendor, shop or creator listing, lowercase
and without the @. It is the key sourceIndex() builds its map on, so a
handle with no listing yields nothing rather than a bare name.
show    the show's name EXACTLY as data/shows.json spells it.
city    that show's city, also exactly as shows.json spells it. Both are
checked against the calendar on every build and a miss THROWS, because
a typo here would silently drop the badge rather than shout.
why     who said so and when. Not optional.

W1FHYQ8cWlU.why: The owner, 2 September 2026: "you already know who the vendor is we have a vendor page and logo for them so add in cards bought from TOAK Pulls" and "add in that it was bought a a local card show, Collector Fest in Rochester, NY at JCC". The description for this rip says "from TOAK Pulls" as plain text rather than @TOAKPulls, so the automatic credit finds nothing; the show half would have resolved on its own.

38yPPGnA7Vk.why: The owner, 6 September 2026: "Todays video is Chaos Rising, ETB #3, Pack #7, Hit yes - Xerneas - Single Gold Star - Illustration Rare", and separately "todays rip is a pack bought from LingSter Games". LingSterGames is the YouTube handle on their /shops.html listing, which is the key sourceIndex() maps on. No show and no city: this was bought over a shop counter on West Ridge Road, not at a card show, and those two fields are the show gate rather than an address.

9TCFBLckSRs.why: The owner, 15 September 2026: "This is also a box bought at LingSter Games so we can tag them on the page for it". The eighth pack of the same Chaos Rising ETB #3 he bought from them, whose seventh is the entry above. THE AUTOMATIC JOIN GENUINELY MISSES THIS ONE and was tested rather than assumed: the description reads "an awesome box from our friends at @lingstergames", and "from our friends at @" is none of shared/pack-source.mjs's phrases -- its pattern wants "from @" directly, so packSource() returns null on this text and returns the shop the moment this pin exists. Loosening the regex to "at @" was the alternative and is refused for the reason written in that file: "go follow @X" and a real credit are the same string to a handle search, and his own word is the better source. No show and no city: bought over the counter on West Ridge Road, not at a card show, and those two fields are the show gate rather than an address.
